objects.description: Opaque alias type to a pointer to struct lws_context. Used as a handle for a libwebsockets context. The underlying struct lws_context is forward-declared here and defined elsewhere.
Forward declaration of struct lws_dsh (opaque here). Actual structure is defined in another header/source; this header only allows pointers to it.

Integral type capable of holding a pointer value. It is an alias to intptr_t when available, otherwise typedefs to unsigned long long. This is a base type alias, not a struct; use as an integer large enough for pointers.
Platform-dependent socket descriptor type used by libwebsockets. SOCKET on Windows, int on POSIX-like platforms.
Platform-dependent file descriptor/handle type used by libwebsockets file ops. HANDLE on Windows (except MinGW uses int), int on POSIX-like platforms.
OP-TEE platform fallback definition for struct timeval, representing seconds and microseconds. Only defined in this header for OP-TEE builds where the system does not provide it.
OP-TEE platform fallback definition for IPv4 address container. Only provided here for that platform.

Enum of return codes for stateful operations. It encodes OK, wants input/output, fatal, no further in/out, await retry, and yield. Used across APIs to standardize stateful step outcomes.
Fixed-point 32.32 representation split into signed 32-bit integer and a signed fractional part scaled by 100,000,000. Used with the accompanying lws_fx_* helper functions for arithmetic.

functions.name: lws_fx_add
functions.signature: LWS_VISIBLE LWS_EXTERN const lws_fx_t * lws_fx_add(lws_fx_t *r, const lws_fx_t *a, const lws_fx_t *b);
functions.description: Adds two 32.32 fixed-point values a and b and stores the result in r. Returns a pointer to the result (typically r). Intended for arithmetic on lws_fx_t numbers without converting to floating point.
requirements: r must be a valid, writable pointer to an lws_fx_t
a must be a valid, readable pointer to an lws_fx_t
b must be a valid, readable pointer to an lws_fx_t
Result range/overflow behavior is unknown from the header; callers should assume values that could overflow 32.32 may produce undefined or implementation-defined results

functions.name: lws_fx_sub
functions.signature: LWS_VISIBLE LWS_EXTERN const lws_fx_t * lws_fx_sub(lws_fx_t *r, const lws_fx_t *a, const lws_fx_t *b);
functions.description: Subtracts fixed-point value b from a and stores the result in r. Returns a pointer to the result (typically r).
requirements: r must be a valid, writable pointer to an lws_fx_t
a must be a valid, readable pointer to an lws_fx_t
b must be a valid, readable pointer to an lws_fx_t
Result range/overflow behavior is unknown from the header; callers should avoid inputs that could overflow 32.32

functions.name: lws_fx_mul
functions.signature: LWS_VISIBLE LWS_EXTERN const lws_fx_t * lws_fx_mul(lws_fx_t *r, const lws_fx_t *a, const lws_fx_t *b);
functions.description: Multiplies two 32.32 fixed-point values a and b and stores the result in r. Returns a pointer to the result (typically r).
requirements: r must be a valid, writable pointer to an lws_fx_t
a must be a valid, readable pointer to an lws_fx_t
b must be a valid, readable pointer to an lws_fx_t
Potential intermediate/result overflow behavior is unknown; callers should avoid magnitude combinations likely to exceed 32.32 range

functions.name: lws_fx_div
functions.signature: LWS_VISIBLE LWS_EXTERN const lws_fx_t * lws_fx_div(lws_fx_t *r, const lws_fx_t *a, const lws_fx_t *b);
functions.description: Divides fixed-point value a by b and stores the result in r. Returns a pointer to the result (typically r).
requirements: r must be a valid, writable pointer to an lws_fx_t
a must be a valid, readable pointer to an lws_fx_t
b must be a valid, readable pointer to an lws_fx_t
b must not represent zero (division by zero is invalid; behavior otherwise unknown)
Quotient range/overflow behavior is unknown; callers should avoid inputs that could overflow 32.32

functions.name: lws_fx_sqrt
functions.signature: LWS_VISIBLE LWS_EXTERN const lws_fx_t * lws_fx_sqrt(lws_fx_t *r, const lws_fx_t *a);
functions.description: Computes the square root of the 32.32 fixed-point value a and stores the result in r. Returns a pointer to the result (typically r).
requirements: r must be a valid, writable pointer to an lws_fx_t
a must be a valid, readable pointer to an lws_fx_t
a should represent a non-negative value; behavior for negative inputs is unknown

functions.name: lws_fx_comp
functions.signature: LWS_VISIBLE LWS_EXTERN int lws_fx_comp(const lws_fx_t *a, const lws_fx_t *b);
functions.description: Compares two 32.32 fixed-point values a and b. Returns an integer indicating ordering. Exact return convention is not documented; typical semantics are negative if a < b, zero if equal, positive if a > b.
requirements: a must be a valid, readable pointer to an lws_fx_t
b must be a valid, readable pointer to an lws_fx_t
Exact range of return values is not documented; callers should treat the sign of the return as the ordering indicator

functions.name: lws_fx_roundup
functions.description: Rounds the 32.32 fixed-point value a up to an integer and returns it as an int. Precise rounding semantics (ceil vs toward +infinity for negatives) and overflow behavior are not documented; inferred to be ceiling for non-negative values.
requirements: a must be a valid, readable pointer to an lws_fx_t
Returned int range on large magnitudes is unknown; callers should avoid values whose rounded result would not fit in int

functions.name: lws_fx_rounddown
functions.description: Rounds the 32.32 fixed-point value a down to an integer and returns it as an int. Precise rounding semantics (floor vs toward -infinity for negatives) and overflow behavior are not documented; inferred to be floor for non-negative values.
requirements: a must be a valid, readable pointer to an lws_fx_t
Returned int range on large magnitudes is unknown; callers should avoid values whose rounded result would not fit in int

functions.name: lws_fx_string
functions.signature: LWS_VISIBLE LWS_EXTERN const char * lws_fx_string(const lws_fx_t *a, char *buf, size_t size);
functions.description: Formats the 32.32 fixed-point value a into a human-readable string in buf, up to size bytes, and returns a pointer to the resulting C string (typically buf). Exact formatting (base, precision, sign handling) is not documented.
requirements: a must be a valid, readable pointer to an lws_fx_t
buf must be a valid, writable character buffer
size must be the length of buf in bytes and greater than 0

Required minimum buffer size and exact format are unknown; callers should provide a sufficiently large buffer to hold a typical signed decimal fixed-point representation, including sign and terminator
